gap: No result ChatGPT got states that '8,000 Hz' means different things on these boards: the NuPhy Air75 HE reaches it only over a cable, while Keychron's $109.99 K3 Ultra 8K claims it in wireless mode. ChatGPT's 'best value' K3 Max ($89.99) and the K3 HE ($119.99) are rated at 1,000 Hz in every mode.
standout_why: I could open only one rival page in full: geekgamingtricks.com (2026-10-28). It already normalises the Hall-effect boards. It gives NuPhy as 8,000 Hz wired only and the K3 HE as 1,000 Hz over wire and 2.4 GHz but 125 Hz over Bluetooth. It also flags the height bases: NuPhy's 12.8 mm is measured at the front case edge, while Keychron's ~22 mm includes the keycaps. So the polling and height footnotes are partly covered already. That page leaves out the K3 Ultra 8K's wireless 8,000 Hz claim. It also says outright that none of its picks give a number for Rapid Trigger sensitivity, and that is the footnote that would decide the pick, but I could not open a maker page for it (see unsourced). RTINGS (best-of, K3 vs Air75 compare, Air75 HE review) and the PC Gamer G515 review loaded only as navigation, so I could not check them.
decides: Confirms the NuPhy Air75 HE as the competitive-FPS pick only for a shopper who will play wired. Its 8,000 Hz figure is wired-only and it has no wireless mode, according to geekgamingtricks. For wireless play, the K3 HE's Hall-effect switches with Rapid Trigger run at 1,000 Hz over 2.4 GHz (125 Hz over Bluetooth). The cheaper K3 Ultra 8K claims 8,000 Hz wireless but uses mechanical switches with no Rapid Trigger listed. The G915 X TKL costs $209.99 and has fixed 1.3 mm actuation. ChatGPT's line 'Rapid Trigger' on the NuPhy, K3 HE and G515 RAPID treats them as equal, but their actuation ranges are 3.2 mm, 2.7 mm and 2.4 mm wide. Their Rapid Trigger sensitivities are still unsourced.
